function.name: create_Recommender_Model
function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

message.content: Below is a practical, step‑by‑step guide you can follow to build a modern, maintainable, and high‑performing front‑end for your e‑commerce site. Feel free to skip or reorder sections based on your team’s experience and the specific requirements of your project. --- ## 1️⃣ Define the Scope & Gather Requirements | What | Why it matters | |------|----------------| | **Target audience** | Determines device mix, accessibility needs, and visual style. | | **Core features** | Product catalog, search, filters, cart, checkout, user account, reviews, admin panel, etc. | | **Performance goals** | Page load time, Time‑to‑Interactive (TTI), First Contentful Paint (FCP). | | **SEO & Analytics** | Structured data, meta tags, Google Analytics, Hotjar. | | **Compliance** | GDPR, PCI‑DSS, WCAG 2.1 AA. | > **Tip:** Create a “feature backlog” and prioritize items into *Must‑Have*, *Nice‑To‑Have*, and *Future* buckets. --- ## 2️⃣ Choose Your Tech Stack | Category | Options | Pros | Cons | |----------|---------|------|------| | **Framework** | React, Vue, Angular, Svelte | Mature ecosystems, component reusability | Learning curve, bundle size | | **State Management** | Redux Toolkit / Zustand / Pinia / NgRx | Predictable global state | Boilerplate overhead | | **Routing** | React Router / Vue Router / Angular Router | Declarative navigation | Requires extra config | | **Styling** | CSS Modules / TailwindCSS / Styled‑Components / SCSS | Scoped styles, utility‑first | Build complexity | | **Build Tool** | Vite / Webpack / Rollup | Fast dev server, tree‑shaking | Configuration depth | | **Testing** | Jest + Testing Library / Cypress | Unit + E2E coverage | Test maintenance | | **CI/CD** | GitHub Actions / GitLab CI / CircleCI | Automation, reproducibility | Setup effort | ### Recommendation for a typical e‑commerce store | Layer | Suggested Tool | |-------|----------------| | **UI Framework** | React (with Next.js for SSR) | | **State** | Redux Toolkit (RTK Query for API) | | **Styling** | TailwindCSS + CSS Modules | | **Testing** | Jest + React Testing Library + Cypress | | **Deployment** | Vercel / Netlify (static + edge functions) | > **Why Next.js?** It gives you server‑side rendering out of the box, which is great for SEO and initial page speed. --- ## 3️⃣ Design Phase 1. **Wireframes** – Sketch low‑fidelity screens for key pages (Home, Category, Product Detail, Cart, Checkout, Account). 2. **High‑Fidelity Mockups** – Use Figma/Adobe XD to create pixel‑perfect designs. Include: - Brand colors, typography, iconography - Responsive breakpoints (mobile, tablet, desktop) - Component states (hover, active, disabled) 3. **Component Library** – Build reusable UI primitives (Button, Input, Card, Modal, Tooltip). Document them in Storybook. 4. **Accessibility Audit** – Ensure contrast ratios, ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, focus order. --- ## 4️⃣ Project Skeleton ```bash my-ecom-store/ ├─ public/ # Static assets (images, favicon) ├─ src/ │ ├─ app/ # App entry point, router, layout │ ├─ features/ # Feature folders (products, cart, auth) │ │ ├─ products/ │ │ │ ├─ api.ts │ │ │ ├─ slice.ts │ │ │ └─ components/ │ │ └─ cart/ │ ├─ shared/ # Reusable components, hooks, utils │ ├─ styles/ # Global Tailwind config, CSS modules │ ├─ tests/ # Jest + Cypress test files │ └─ index.tsx ├─ .env # Environment variables ├─ tailwind.config.js ├─ postcss.config.js └─ package.json ``` > **Folder‑per‑Feature** keeps code modular and easier to scale. --- ## 5️⃣ Core Implementation Steps ### 5.1 Set Up the Development Environment ```bash npx create-next-app@latest my-ecom-store --typescript cd my-ecom-store npm install @reduxjs/toolkit react-redux @tanstack/react-query tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer npx tailwindcss init -p ``` Configure `tailwind.config.js`: ```js module.exports = { content: [ "./src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}", ], theme: { extend: {} }, plugins: [], } ``` Add Tailwind directives to `globals.css`. ### 5.2 Configure State & API Layer ```ts // src/features/products/api.ts import { createApi, fetchBaseQuery } from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'; export const productApi = createApi({ reducerPath: 'productApi', baseQuery: fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: '/api' }), endpoints: (builder) => ({ getProducts: builder.query({ query: () => 'products', }), getProductById: builder.query({ query: (id) => `products/${id}`, }), }), }); export const { useGetProductsQuery, useGetProductByIdQuery } = productApi; ``` Add the API middleware to the store: ```ts // src/app/store.ts import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit'; import { productApi } from '../features/products/api'; export const store = configureStore({ reducer: { [productApi.reducerPath]: productApi.reducer, }, middleware: (getDefaultMiddleware) => getDefaultMiddleware().concat(productApi.middleware), }); ``` ### 5.3 Build Reusable Components ```tsx // src/shared/components/Button.tsx interface ButtonProps extends React.ButtonHTMLAttributes { variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'outline';
